title: Do sub folders improve loading time of images?

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Hi all,
I'm working on a kind of picture heavy game. Sometimes, there is a noticeable delay in loading pictures. E.g. when you open a character menu, the player artworks might be loaded in a second later.
I guess the game works through the whole img/pictures folder, searching for the requested image.
Would it help to work with sub folders, to split up the amount of images to check per request?
Or wouldn't that matter much, since the game would check the entire pictures anyway, or the delay has other reasons?
Since it's very risky to change all the picture paths afterwards, I'd like to be sure, this actually might solve the issue.
Thanks,
Zia

posts.author: inc0der
posts.body:
Subfolder likely won't make a difference, unless you have an actual plugin that is scanning the directory everytime you open the menu, which is unlikely. An image is loaded with the direct url/filepath, so it's not reading a directory it's simply reading the file right away.
Usually performance issues like you describe are caused by large images, if the images are used often, then it may be a good idea to preload the images when your game boots up.
You can check out Synrec's preloader to help you with that
https://synrec.itch.io/rpg-maker-mz-preloader

posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
are we talking a compiled game or the test build?
if it's compiled, it could be that the system takes a little longer to decode the package, every time.
if it's an HDD, it could be badly fragmented.
anyway, any on-the-fly heavy image processing should use a preloader... especially with your size of image, it would get rid of any loading time while playing. Just load the whole bunch in memory one time, and keep it there.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Zia_ said:
Code:
var variableValue = $gameVariables.value(1105); // Check value of v1105
var imageName = "TradingCard_" + variableValue; // Create file name based on variable
ImageManager.loadPicture(imageName);
Click to expand...
The first line is unnecessary, and is inaccurate - it's not checking anything, it's just declaring a variable.
You could simply do
Code:
var imageName = "TradingCard_" + $gameVariables.value(1105);
(of course, you also don't need the imageName variable and could just put all of that as the argument for ImageManager).
Also, just calling ImageManager.loadPicture() doesn't change anything unless you're doing it at an actual different time than when you're trying to display the image. You'd need to set something equal to its return value in order to have it wait for the loading to complete. (as far as I know)
This should be done internally by default, inside the drawFace() method - are you using a plugin to customize your menu? If yes, I would suggest fixing the plugin rather than trying to find ways to work around the issue.

posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
@Zia_
you don't really need a preloader plugin per se, if you're not concerned about memory leaks.
you can put a loop at the beginning of the program to just bulk-load all images into memory, and another one at the end before shutdown to clear the memory.
the plugin just gives you the chance to fine-tune what you load, and when.
